title: Rent vs Buy Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Rent vs Buy Calculator: Compare the monthly cost of renting with buying the same home — mortgage, rent and equity. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it,…
content:
The [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Compare the monthly cost of renting with buying the same home — mortgage, rent and equity. Enter your monthly rent, home price, down payment, mortgage rate, mortgage term and years you will stay and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Compare renting with buying the same home, side by side. The calculator works out the monthly mortgage payment on the home price minus your down payment, compares it with the rent, and shows what happens over the years you plan to stay — including the part people forget: every mortgage payment pays down principal, so a buyer builds equity while a renter's payments are gone for good. This comparison excludes property tax, insurance, maintenance and changes in home prices, so treat it as a starting point, not a final answer.

## How to use the Rent vs Buy Calculator

Start by entering your monthly rent, then entering your home price, entering your down payment, entering your mortgage rate (%), entering your mortgage term (years) and finally entering your years you will stay. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the monthly rent for a comparable home.
2. Enter the home price, your down payment, the mortgage rate and term.
3. Enter how many years you expect to stay.
4. Compare the monthly payments — then look at the equity line, which is what renting never gives you.

## Formula

Monthly mortgage = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan amount, r the monthly rate and n the number of payments. Equity after k months = down payment + principal repaid.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Renting at $2,000 a month versus buying a $400,000 home with $80,000 down at 6.5% for 30 years: the mortgage is $2,022.62 a month — only $22.62 more than rent. After 5 years you will have paid $121,357.06 in mortgage payments versus $120,000 in rent, but you will have $100,444.87 of equity. Try the same figures in the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Monthly rent: 2000, Home price: 400000, Down payment: 80000, Mortgage rate: 6.5 %, Mortgage term: 30 years, Years you will stay: 5), the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) returns Monthly mortgage payment: $2,022.62, Monthly rent: $2,000, Mortgage minus rent (monthly): $22.62, Total rent over 5 years: $120,000, Total mortgage payments over 5 years: $121,357.06, Principal paid off: $20,444.87, Your equity after that time: $100,444.87. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## What the monthly payment leaves out

The mortgage payment here is principal and interest only. A real monthly housing cost also includes property tax, homeowner's insurance and usually PMI if your down payment is under 20%, plus maintenance — roughly 1% of the home's value a year. Rent, by contrast, is usually the whole housing cost. Add those ownership costs before deciding the two are close.

## Why how long you stay decides it

Buying has large upfront costs — closing costs, moving, furnishing — that only pay off if you stay. In the first years of a mortgage almost every payment is interest, so little equity builds. As a rule of thumb, buying usually wins if you will stay at least five to seven years; under that, renting often comes out ahead once all the costs are counted.

## Equity is the renter's missing line

A renter's $120,000 over five years buys nothing lasting. A buyer paying a similar amount ends the same five years owning a share of the home — in the example, $100,444.87 of equity from the down payment plus principal repaid. That is the strongest argument for buying, and it is the line this calculator exists to show.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Always add tax, insurance and maintenance to the mortgage before comparing with rent.
- If you might move within a few years, renting usually wins — buying costs take years to recover.
- A bigger down payment cuts both the monthly payment and the interest paid over the life of the loan.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is it cheaper to rent or buy?

It depends on the prices, the mortgage rate and how long you stay. This calculator compares the monthly payments and the equity built — buying usually wins over 5–7+ years in one place, renting usually wins for short stays or very expensive markets. Try it with your own numbers in the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does this calculator include property tax and insurance?

No — the mortgage payment is principal and interest only. Add your local property tax, homeowner's insurance and maintenance (roughly 1% of the home's value a year) to the buying side for a fair comparison. Try it with your own numbers in the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is equity and why does it matter?

Equity is the part of the home you own: your down payment plus the principal you have repaid. Rent builds no equity at all, which is why two similar monthly payments can still leave the buyer far ahead after five years. Try it with your own numbers in the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Rent vs Buy Calculator use?

Monthly mortgage = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan amount, r the monthly rate and n the number of payments. Equity after k months = down payment + principal repaid. You can see it in action in the [Rent vs Buy Calculator](/rent-vs-buy-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
